before: Would have created a sales and use tax exemption framework for data centers.
after: Would create a sales and use tax exemption for eligible data center property and equipment, subject to investment, employment and reporting conditions; the adopted free conference report also proposed a remote-worker income tax credit.
Engrossed proposal would limit the data center exemption to purchases through 2051-06-30; vetoed. Confirm this provision against the adopted free conference report.

before: Kentucky Ratepayer Protection Act; would require PSC-approved tariffs or contracts for data center loads over 100 MW and assign new infrastructure costs to the data center customer.
after: Kentucky Ratepayer Protection Act: would require PSC-approved tariffs or contracts for greater than 100 MW in aggregated qualifying new contract capacity; exclusively serving facilities' costs would be assigned to the customer and shared-benefit costs allocated proportionally, with a conditional existing-load exception.

before: Would require data center electric service contracts and tariffs, $75,000 minimum application fees, cost studies, dedicated resource rules for large loads, and protections against shifting electric, water, wastewater, and gas infrastructure costs to other customers.
after: House-passed substitute would require qualifying data center electric service contracts, tariffs, at least $75,000 initial application fees and studies; dedicated resources for projected peak loads over 25 MW for municipal utilities and over 250 MW for regulated retail suppliers; and gas, water and wastewater cost protections, with section-specific exceptions.

before: Amended KRS 154.20-220 to allow incentives for data centers locating in areas with specified population thresholds.
after: Amended KRS 154.20-220 to remove the prior 500,000-population consolidated-government location requirement and add county-population-based minimum investments for owners, operators, and colocation tenants in the qualified data center incentive program.

before: Enacted as Acts Ch. 166; filed with Secretary of State 2024-04-12 after House ruled Governor's line-item vetoes invalid
after: Became law without Governor's signature 2024-04-10; House ruled two line-item vetoes invalid and filed with Secretary of State 2024-04-12 (Acts Ch. 166)

before: Sen. Gex Williams (KY Senate Republican) [VERIFY: original SB 197 sponsor list not separately retrieved; Williams identified through bill record]
after: P. Wheeler; S. Madon; S. Funke Frommeyer; R. Mills; R. Webb

before: SB 197 is the state government agencies budget/appropriations vehicle bill ('AN ACT providing funding and establishing conditions for state government agencies and institutions, making an appropriation therefor, and declaring an emergency'), not a standalone data-center policy bill. House Committee Substitute 1 (2026-03-27) inserted HB 593-style data center electric-service provisions for municipal electric utilities: application/tariff process, $75,000 minimum nonrefundable application fee, 25 MW dedicated-resource threshold, prohibition on subsidizing data center customers via non-data-center rates, and curtailment-allocation rules. That language does not appear in House Committee Substitute 2 (2026-04-15), the version that actually passed both chambers, or in the final enacted bill text. SB 197 was enacted as Acts Ch. 202 (with Governor line-item vetoes of unrelated appropriations items) but contains no data center provisions in its final form.
after: SB 197 originated as a county-tiered economic-development incentives bill and became a supplemental appropriations vehicle. HCS1, reported March 27, proposed data-center electric-service rules for municipal utilities and retail suppliers, including contracts, tariffs, cost allocation and curtailment; for municipal utilities the application included an initial nonrefundable fee of at least $75,000 and information on a proposed dedicated resource when contract capacity exceeds 25 MW. HCS2 passed both chambers April 15; neither its retained text nor the enrolled text contains a 'data center' text match. The retained comparison does not determine whether similar rules became law elsewhere.

before: Would require decommissioning plans and financial security for data centers over 50 MW on land taxed as agricultural land within the prior 10 years, and would add energy and water efficiency engagement terms to incentive agreements.
after: Would require a decommissioning plan and financial security before operation for data centers with actual or expected monthly peak electric load over 50 MW, including affiliated and commonly owned loads, on land valued and taxed as agricultural at any time in the 10 years before construction; incentive memoranda executed after the proposed effective date would require local engagement on energy efficiency and water conservation.

before: Would limit data center nondisclosure and confidentiality agreements by public agencies, void provisions expanding secrecy beyond Kentucky open-records and open-meetings law, and require disclosure of project owner, location, incentives, utility demand, water use, infrastructure upgrades, and mitigation commitments.
after: Would limit public-agency data center confidentiality agreements and void certain open-records or open-meetings waivers in contracts entered after the proposed effective date; specified project actions would trigger disclosure of ownership, location, incentives, aggregate utility demand, water use, infrastructure and mitigation, subject to a trade-secret exception.
